issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch for Animal: the UML in the problem statement specifies a constructor Animal(String, int) (name and age), but the provided solution implements Animal with a single-parameter constructor Animal(String). This inconsistency can confuse students about whether to implement an age attribute and a two-argument constructor, and may cause tests or instructor expectations to differ from student implementations.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor requirement consistent across artifacts. Either update the UML and problem text to require only Animal(String) (remove age), or update the solution and template to implement Animal(String, int) and initialize an age attribute (with corresponding getter/setter). Ensure the problem statement, template, and reference solution all show the same constructor signature.

issues.description: Attribute mismatch for Animal: the UML in the problem statement lists two attributes (name: String and age: int), but the solution's Animal class only declares a name attribute and omits age. This creates ambiguity about whether students should implement an age field and its getter/setter.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the attribute list between the problem statement and code. Either include age:int in the solution's Animal class (with constructor parameter, getter and setter) to match the UML, or remove age from the UML and the textual description so that only name remains. Update all artifacts (UML, textual tasks, template, and solution) accordingly.

issues.description: The problem statement's UML and text explicitly define Animal as having attributes 'name' and 'age' and a constructor Animal(String, int) (i.e., two-argument constructor). The solution implementation provides Animal(String) (single-argument) and omits the 'age' attribute and its accessor methods. This mismatch between the required constructor/attribute in the problem specification and the identifier/signature present in the solution creates a mapping confusion: students expect to implement or use Animal(String, int) and 'age' but the provided solution uses a different constructor signature and field set.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the implementation with the problem UML: update the Animal class in the solution to include a private int age field, provide getter and setter for age, and implement a two-argument constructor Animal(String name, int age) that initializes both fields. Alternatively, if the intended design is a single-argument constructor, update the problem statement/UML to reflect Animal(String) and remove the 'age' attribute to keep artifacts consistent.
